study type: secondary analysis of cross-sectional survey data
outcome: newborn care practices (defined as completing at least 2 out of 6 signal functions: cord examination, temperature measurement, danger sign counseling, breastfeeding counseling, breastfeeding observation, and weight measurement) within 48 hours of life
cohort: The study utilized data from 3936 mothers from the Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey 2017-2018.
finding: Wealth, C-sections, institutional births, skilled birth attendants, and frequent antenatal care visits were significantly associated with a higher likelihood of receiving at least two recommended newborn care signal functions.
mod_finding: Mothers who had C-sections were 2.46 times more likely to have their newborns receive at least two signal functions of newborn care within 48 hours of birth.
